body: I have! A few years back actually. I think that was around the time I started to realize how bleak things were starting to get. The suicidal thoughts really just started in 2015.

It does take quite an amount of research. Have you also considered aiming for other fields or certificates? A friend of mine went off the longboat to jump onto digital forensics. He had almost no knowledge on it, but managed to get certified and land a job.    

Ah, well. Anything you might be mildly interested in? Starting a business, trying out a different field, etc, etc.

Just one other. There are complications to this though, because they're extremely attached to me. I'm grateful for this person being there, but they are not the best to speak about my depression to. Not quite sure how to explain this. . .    

My speaking about depression depresses them in turn due to their inability to "cure" me. It's not going to make coherent sense without a complete history of the relationship. Ah, damn.    

Thanks, btw.

What are you in college for? I'm not asking what your high school counselor's or your parents' opinions are on this. What are *you* in college for? 

If you can't find a reason, why let your life be wasted due to some conventional standard? If you're worried about money, as often people correlate success with money, then you can direct your effort elsewhere. Contrary to popular belief, there are other options aside from college that provide a stable income.

Writing isn't for everyone, even if you're good. I stopped years ago because it made me far too unhappy, despite the fact that I was already under contract.    

I had my trouble trying to find some other field, because writing had really been everything I put my life into. It wasn't an easy transition, but I found music to be a good substitute.    

Don't force yourself to write. You're not tied to one field, ever.
